contexts.lucas-align: Lucas Align public context and demo positioning: technology built around people; custom software; AI solutions; workflow automation; Wraparound Care Communities; foster/adoptive/kinship and vulnerable-family support; volunteers; lead volunteers; church advocates; county coordinators/admins; support tasks; schedules; permissions; reporting; security and stewardship. Strong answers should be concise and human-centered. Focus on the vision: families receiving timely care, volunteers knowing how to help, churches and partners staying coordinated, and leaders stewarding the work responsibly. Avoid sounding technical unless the question asks for technical detail.
contexts.traillife-pa-2301: Trail Life Troop PA 2301 context for grant drafting. EIN: 23-3046329. Tax exempt no.: 75435237. Trail Life USA mission from official FAQ: guide generations of courageous young men to honor God, lead with integrity, serve others, and experience outdoor adventure. Vision: produce godly and responsible husbands, fathers, and citizens. Trail Life is church-based, Christ-centered, and boy-focused. The program uses outdoor adventure, adult mentoring, patrol-style participation, service, advancement, and leadership opportunities to help boys grow in character, faith, purpose, practical skills, and servant leadership. Official program branches include Outdoor Skills, Life Skills, Heritage, Hobbies, Values, Science & Technology, and Sports & Fitness. Troops are owned, operated, and shepherded by a local church or Christian charter organization. Parents are encouraged to be involved, and adult leaders are subject to child safety and youth protection training/background checks. Grant answers should be direct, concise, and focused on local troop impact: boys gaining positive mentors, outdoor experiences, leadership opportunities, service habits, character formation, faith development, and practical skills. For LGBTQ+, gender identity, nondiscrimination, and cultural-belief questions, answer with biblical conviction and Christian charity: every person has dignity and should be treated with kindness and respect; the troop does not demean or mistreat people who disagree; the program remains faithful to its Christian beliefs and boy-focused standards; leaders should be gracious, clear, and unwavering rather than argumentative or judgmental. Avoid hostile language, culture-war rhetoric, slurs, contempt, or claims that attack people. Avoid mixing in Lucas Align, foster care, Wraparound Care Communities, or unrelated software language.

Title: Training for Aspiring Entrepreneurs - Emerging Entrepreneurs Academy
Training for Aspiring Entrepreneurs - Emerging Entrepreneurs Academy HOME ABOUT DONATE SPONSORS PHOTOS & VIDEOS IN THE NEWS APPLY CONTACT EXPO & BANQUET CONTACT US EMERGING ENTREPRENEURS ACADEMY An exclusive program for high school students interested in learning about and experiencing the life of an entrepreneur! The Emerging Entrepreneurs Academy is an intensive 6-week entrepreneur workshop that is developing the Berks County business leaders of tomorrow. Please consider sponsoring a high school student in your school district. Sponsor a Dream Chaser. When they succeed we all win! CONTACT US TO LEARN HOW ABOUT THE PROGRAM Students who have an interest in someday owning a business will gain valuable insight and knowledge in recognizing opportunities and understanding the challenges of owning a business… directly from local entrepreneurs. This interactive 6-week summer curriculum delivers a unique combination of educational workshops along with a internship-like experience for greater guidance to career decision making. Outcomes and Takeaways Students will have a better understanding of the real world of being an Entrepreneur and business owner. They will be taught by exceptional, real-world, practicing entrepreneurs sharing stories of successes and failures. The students will participate in role-playing and interactive activities as well as three (3) weeks of hands-on, in-the-field training. Each student will receive a binder to collect all of the information they will receive as well as other resources. This material can be accessed for years to come. They will have a better understanding of what owning a business is really about and whether or not this might be the career path they want to pursue. Evaluation Criteria During the classroom week, students will draft questions about the topics discussed to pose to the business owner during their internship week. After spending time in the business, students will then be required to submit a paper answering the questions. There will be a total of 3 papers. DID YOU KNOW? 60% of teens want to launch their own business! STUDENT APPLICATION Must be in 10th, 11th or 12th grade Emerging Entrepreneurs Academy is a joint effort by Career Ready Berks in cooperation with the Small Business Resource Association. Learn more PROGRAM DETAILS WHO CAN PARTICIPATE? The EEA is a 6-week summer program for 10th, 11th and 12th grade students who have an interest in some day starting and owning a business.
